subject: Nanotechnology
title: Electron Microscopy
description: A quick win: understand Electron Microscopy.

hook.text: Light microscopes hit a wall at 200 nanometers — electrons smash through with 1000x better resolution.

buildup.text: A TEM fires electrons through ultra-thin samples, revealing detail invisible to any light microscope.

discovery.text: Scanning electron microscopes bounce electrons off surfaces, building 3D images of nanoscale shapes.

twist.text: Electron microscopes need vacuum chambers — you cannot watch living cells in real time.

climax.text: Cryo-EM solved this by flash-freezing samples — earning a Nobel Prize in 2017.

punchline.text: Swap photons for electrons and the nanoscale appears.

quiz.question: Why can electron microscopes see smaller features than light microscopes?
options: Electrons have much shorter wavelengths than visible light
